cards.title: THE ENTRYWAY
cards.tagline: FIVE ZONES. START AT THE DOOR.
cards.objective: The entryway is five small places, not one big job. This card is the map and the order.
zones_in_order: EYZ-005 Door, Mat, and Immediate Floor
cards.start_here: EYZ-005 Door, Mat, and Immediate Floor. Do the Door, Mat, and Immediate Floor first. It is the shortest zone in the room, it gives you somewhere to stand while you work the other four, and the change shows on the hallway floor within a week.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the five ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your entryway. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do EYA-013 The Full Rebuild Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers every hook, shelf and door in the room.

cards.title: LANDING ZONE
cards.tagline: ONE VERDICT PER SHEET. NOTHING RETURNS UNDECIDED.
cards.objective: The spot where pockets empty on the way in and refill on the way out.
callouts: One tray holding keys and sunglasses
One wallet and one phone per adult
A single folder standing upright, fewer than ten sheets
Bare surface on both sides of the tray
Charging dock clear of the drip line under the hooks
No loose paper anywhere on the surface
cards.done_looks_like: One tray holding keys and sunglasses, one wallet and one phone per adult, a single upright folder with fewer than ten sheets of paper standing in it, and bare surface on both sides of the tray.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: Wet umbrellas and rain-soaked sleeves drip onto whatever sits directly below the hooks. If the charging dock or a power strip is under that line, move it out of the drip.

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: A phone dock, a lamp and a plug-in heater chained together behind the console is the overload that starts here. One dock, one outlet, nothing chained.

the_call.title: The paper with no verdict
the_call.text: What you have been avoiding here is not the keys, it is the six sheets of paper you keep shifting from one end of the surface to the other. They stay because each needs a small unpleasant action: a form, a phone call, a payment. The rule is that nothing returns to the surface without a verdict, and there are only three: act, file, recycle. If it is act, it stands upright in the folder with the date written in the corner. When any item in that folder passes fourteen days, it stops being paperwork and becomes a decision. Do it tonight, or accept honestly that you never will and recycle it. Both of those are answers. Leaving it on the surface is not.

cards.title: COAT AND OUTERWEAR ZONE
cards.tagline: TWO EMPTY HOOKS, ALWAYS. COUNTED BY WEATHER, NOT BY NUMBER.
cards.objective: Hold the outerwear you will actually wear this week, at the moment you reach for it.
callouts: One coat per person on the rail
One bag hanging, not stacked on the floor
Hats and gloves together in one labeled bin
Umbrellas standing upright in the stand
At least two hooks left empty
Nothing weighty stored above head height
cards.done_looks_like: One coat per person on the rail, one bag, hats and gloves together in a single labeled bin on the shelf above, umbrellas standing in the stand, and at least two hooks left empty.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A bin of boots or a heavy holdall stored above head height on the coat shelf lands on whoever tugs the coat underneath it. Weight goes low, light bulky things go high.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A rail loaded past what its brackets were fixed for sags first and lets go later, usually while somebody is standing directly beneath it.

the_call.title: The coat you feel guilty about
the_call.text: Somewhere on this rail is a good coat that cost real money and goes outside roughly never. It survives every clear-out because getting rid of it feels like admitting to the money. The rule is that coats are counted by weather, not by number. Each person gets one coat per kind of weather your climate genuinely produces: wet, cold, and something in between. A second coat in the same category has to beat the first one on a specific, nameable day. If you cannot name that day, that is the coat that leaves. The expensive one is not exempt, because the money is already spent whether it hangs here or keeps someone else warm. Give it one trial: front hook, most reachable spot, two weeks. If you did not reach for it, you have your answer and you had it before you started.

cards.title: SHOE AND BOOT ZONE
cards.tagline: TWO PAIRS PER PERSON. THE SOLE DECIDES, NOT THE MEMORY.
cards.objective: Hold the footwear that comes off at the door, and keep the grit it carried in off every other floor in the house.
callouts: Two pairs per person on the rack, soles down
Boots standing upright in the tray
One pair of slippers per person
A full stride of bare floor between door and rack
Shoe care solvents stored up and out of reach
Nothing loose on the floor beside the rack
cards.done_looks_like: Two pairs per person on the rack, soles down, boots standing in the tray, one pair of slippers each, and a clear stretch of floor a full stride wide between the door and the rack.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Shoes left inside the arc of the door swing are the reason people go down while carrying bags with both hands. That strip of floor stays clear at full stride width, permanently.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Polish, suede cleaner and waterproofing spray are solvents, and they usually sit in an open basket at exactly toddler height. Move shoe care up onto a shelf or out of the room.

the_call.title: The worn out pair you keep for the garden
the_call.text: Everyone has a pair with the tread rubbed smooth that survives on the grounds that it is fine for mucky jobs. Count them honestly and there are usually three such pairs and about one muddy job a year. The rule is that the sole decides, not the memory. Turn the shoe over. If the tread has gone smooth or the heel has worn through on the outer edge, that shoe is no longer safe on a wet step or a slick pavement, which means it is not gardening footwear, it is rubbish with sentimental value attached. Keep exactly one dirty-job pair per person and store it where the dirty jobs happen, not at the front door. The pair you would be embarrassed to be seen in is not a spare. It is a decision you already made and have not carried out.

cards.title: ENTRY CONSOLE OR BENCH
cards.tagline: THREE ITEMS ON TOP. EMPTY SEAT. EVERY SECTION NAMED.
cards.objective: Somewhere to sit while you lace a boot, and somewhere to set a bag down for thirty seconds.
callouts: Three items or fewer on the top surface
The seat itself bare, nothing set down on it
Drawer sections each holding one named category
The base of the drawer visible between things
Nothing stored here that is not needed at the door
Bench strapped to the wall if it stands on narrow legs
cards.done_looks_like: Three items or fewer on the top, a seat with nothing on it at all, and a drawer where every divided section has one named category and you can see the base of the drawer between things.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A narrow console with drawers is a climbing frame to a three year old, and it comes over forwards with the drawers out. Strap it to the wall and keep the heaviest contents in the bottom drawer.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Loose button batteries, coins and small magnets roll into the back corners of this drawer and it opens at exactly the height a toddler can reach. Batteries go in a lidded tin or out of the room entirely.

the_call.title: What the drawer is for
the_call.text: This drawer becomes the second junk drawer within a month of being emptied. It happens every time, because it is the nearest place to set down something you do not want to carry any further. The decision being avoided is not what to throw away. It is admitting the drawer needs a job at all. The rule: this drawer serves the door and nothing else. One test question per item, would you need this while wearing your shoes, either on the way out or in the first ten seconds back in. Dog lead, yes. Sun cream, yes. Spare car charger, yes. The screwdriver, the birthday candles and the case for a phone you no longer own all fail, and they fail even though they genuinely have nowhere better to live. Find them somewhere better today, in another room, with a name on it. If you do not, they will be back in this drawer by the weekend and so will four of their friends.

cards.title: DOOR, MAT, AND IMMEDIATE FLOOR
cards.tagline: BOTH MATS FLAT. THE SWING STAYS BARE.
cards.objective: Catch grit, water and road salt at the threshold so none of it reaches the rest of the floors.
callouts: Coarse mat outside the door, lying flat
Absorbent mat inside the door, lying flat
No curled corners on either mat
Nothing on the floor inside the door's swing
The door latches on the first push
Hinge screws snug, not loose
cards.done_looks_like: A coarse mat outside the door and an absorbent one inside, both lying dead flat with no curled corners, nothing whatsoever on the floor inside the door's swing, and a door that latches on the first push.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A curled mat edge at a doorway catches the toe of someone stepping in with their eyes on their phone or their arms full. Flat edges, gripped or taped, checked every time you vacuum.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A door with a loose hinge screw or a failing closer swings harder than expected and catches fingers against the frame. Tighten the hinge screws while you are down there with the cloth.

the_call.title: When the mat is finished
the_call.text: A mat looks perfectly fine long after it has stopped working, and the decision being dodged is spending money to replace something that is not visibly broken. So test it instead of looking at it. Walk in from outside on a dry gritty day, wipe your feet the way you actually wipe them, then lift the mat and look at both the floor beneath it and the fibres themselves. A working mat holds grit down inside its pile and drops a clear line of dirt when you shake it out. A finished mat has fibres flattened all in one direction, and the grit sits on top of them and walks straight off on the next pair of shoes. If it fails that test, replace it this month rather than next winter. A worn mat is not saving you anything. It is quietly sanding the finish off every floor between this door and the kitchen.

cards.title: WRONG LOCATION
cards.objective: It is stored somewhere, just not where it is used.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Stand where you use it and count the steps to where it is kept. More than two is the wrong cabinet.

cards.title: INSUFFICIENT CAPACITY
cards.objective: The right storage exists and genuinely cannot hold what belongs in it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Put back only what belongs here. If it still will not close, or still stacks four deep, the capacity is the problem, not the habit.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

cards.title: MISSING STANDARD
cards.objective: Nobody agreed what good looks like, so everybody is right.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask two people what this surface should look like at bedtime. Two answers means there is no standard to keep.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

cards.title: MISSING TRIGGER
cards.objective: The reset is a good intention with nothing to attach it to.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Name the moment it happens. If the answer is "when I get round to it", there is no trigger and it will not survive a bad week.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a front hallway at night lit only by a porch light through the glass, a coat still lying over the end of the rail where it was dropped that morning
must_show: The reset is a good intention with nothing to attach it to.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: SAFETY CONSTRAINT
cards.objective: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Look for the four: a blade your hand would meet, weight above shoulder height, heat beside something that burns, and an unsafe placement near a child's reach.
cards.instruction: This is a Safety problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a narrow entry console with an open drawer of loose batteries and coins at exactly a toddler's reaching height
must_show: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: POOR REPLENISHMENT
cards.objective: Consumables run out unnoticed, and stock ages out of use unseen.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Find the last one of something you use daily. If nothing tells you it is the last one, you will find out at the worst possible moment.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: an empty shoe polish tin standing on an otherwise bare entry console shelf beside a pair of dull leather shoes
must_show: Consumables run out unnoticed, and stock ages out of use unseen.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: UNCLEAR OWNERSHIP
cards.objective: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask who resets this zone. If the honest answer is "whoever gets to it" or two names with no agreement, there is no owner.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a front hallway floor with a pair of shoes, a school bag and a dog lead all left in the same spot, nobody's coat hook nearby claimed
must_show: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: SENTIMENTAL ATTACHMENT
cards.objective: The item is kept for what it represents, not because it is used, and the guilt stalls Sort indefinitely.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask if you would buy this again today for what it does. If the answer is no but you still cannot decide, the hold is sentimental.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a single tailored coat with its price tag still attached hanging untouched at the end of an otherwise ordinary coat rail
must_show: The item is kept for what it represents, not because it is used, and the guilt stalls Sort indefinitely.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: UNRESOLVED DECISION
cards.objective: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Pick up one piece. If your first thought is a verb (pay, sign, call, decide) rather than a place, it needs a decision, not a home.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a slim folder standing upright on an entry console holding a handful of envelopes, one opened envelope with a form half pulled out
must_show: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: DIFFICULT TO CLEAN
cards.objective: Reaching the surface to clean it costs more effort than the rest of the zone combined, so it gets skipped.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Time how long it actually takes to reach and wipe the surface. If it requires moving something first, that cost is why it is skipped.
cards.instruction: This is a Shine problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: the corner of a boot tray pushed hard against a wall, a build-up of dried grit visible in the angle where it meets the skirting board

art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: PERCEPTUAL BLINDNESS
cards.objective: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask someone who does not live here to name what looks out of place. If they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, this is the cause.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a coat rail with one coat hanging crookedly off a bent hook, everything around it otherwise orderly
must_show: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: CLEAR THE TRAY AND THE FOLDER
cards.objective: Empty the tray and the paper stack, give every sheet a verdict, and put back only what belongs.
cards.why_it_matters: Paper with no verdict is the reason this surface fills back up faster than any other reset in the house.
steps: Empty the tray and the paper stack onto the surface, then give every sheet a verdict: act, file, or recycle, before anything goes back.
Anything that needs action stands upright in the folder with the date written in the corner.
Recycle what nobody is going to act on, honestly, rather than restack it.
Return only the tray, holding keys and sunglasses, and the folder, to the bare surface.
cards.victory_condition: One tray holds only keys and sunglasses, and no loose paper sits anywhere on the surface.

art.subject: an entryway console with one tray holding keys and sunglasses and a slim folder standing beside it, the rest of the surface completely bare
must_show: One tray holds only keys and sunglasses, and no loose paper sits anywhere on the surface.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: REBUILD THE LANDING SURFACE
cards.objective: Change the surface so a verdict happens in the moment, not the pile.
cards.why_it_matters: A pocket-emptying spot with no charging dock and no folder invites paper and cables to just sit there.
steps: Stand where your hands actually stop when you walk in, and put the tray there, not wherever it currently sits.
Move the charging dock clear of the drip line under any hooks, onto the outlet nearest the tray.
Set the folder upright at one end of the tray, and write today's date on a card inside it as the first entry.
Coil and clip any charging cable so it lies flat rather than trailing across the surface.
Count what has landed here in the past week that is not keys, sunglasses, a wallet, a phone, or paper, and give each item a home somewhere else in the house.
cards.victory_condition: The tray sits exactly where your hand opens on the way in, the dock is clear of the drip line, and everything on the surface is one of the five named things.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: an entryway console with a shallow tray positioned right at hand height by the door, a charging dock plugged into an outlet well clear of the hooks above, its cable coiled flat
must_show: The tray sits exactly where your hand opens on the way in, the dock is clear of the drip line, and everything on the surface is one of the five named things.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR TWO HOOKS
cards.objective: Clear the two hooks nearest the door and confirm every coat still on the rail earns its place this season.
cards.why_it_matters: Two hooks that are never empty are the first sign the rail is carrying coats by number instead of by weather.
inputs: a bin bag or box for coats leaving the room
steps: Take down every coat that did not go outside once this cold season, and clear the two hooks nearest the door.
Carry each coat you took down to a bedroom closet or the giveaway pile, not to the floor.
Space the coats that remain so shoulders do not touch.
cards.victory_condition: Two hooks stand empty nearest the door, and every coat still on the rail was worn this season.

art.subject: a coat rail with two hooks nearest the door standing completely empty and the remaining coats spaced apart along the rest of the rail
must_show: Two hooks stand empty nearest the door, and every coat still on the rail was worn this season.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: REBUILD THE COAT RAIL
cards.objective: Count coats by weather instead of by number, and fix what the rail can actually hold.
cards.why_it_matters: A rail loaded past its bracket weight sags and lets go, usually while somebody stands directly beneath it.
inputs: a bin bag for the giveaway pile
steps: Take every coat off the rail and lay them out where you can see all of them at once.
Sort into the weather categories your climate actually produces: wet, cold, and something in between.
Keep one per person per category. A second coat in the same category has to name a specific day it beats the first, or it goes.
Hang the kept coats back with a visible gap between each, heaviest nearest the door.
Move anything heavy or bulky off the shelf above head height down to a low shelf instead.
cards.victory_condition: At least two hooks stand empty at all times, and nothing heavy sits above head height on the shelf.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a coat rail with a clear gap of bare space between each hanging coat, a shelf above holding only a labeled bin and light hats, nothing heavy visible on it
must_show: At least two hooks stand empty at all times, and nothing heavy sits above head height on the shelf.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: PAIR UP AND CUT TO TWO
cards.objective: Pair every shoe up, and keep only two pairs per person on the rack.
cards.why_it_matters: A pair on the floor instead of the rack is usually a pair the rack was never told it needed to hold.
inputs: nothing beyond fifteen minutes and floor space to sort on
steps: Pull every shoe off the rack, pair them up on the floor, and put back only two pairs per person, soles down.
Set aside anything past two pairs per person for the giveaway pile or another room's closet.
Stand the boot tray's pairs upright rather than laid on their sides.
cards.victory_condition: Two pairs per person stand on the rack, soles down, and the floor between the door and the rack is bare.

art.subject: a shoe rack holding exactly two pairs of shoes per person, each standing sole-down with visible space between pairs, and a bare stretch of floor in front of it
must_show: Two pairs per person stand on the rack, soles down, and the floor between the door and the rack is bare.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: REBUILD THE SHOE RACK
cards.objective: Move shoe care solvents out of toddler reach and fix the rack so it cannot tip.
cards.why_it_matters: Polish and waterproofing spray sitting in an open basket at toddler height are a poisoning risk, and a top-heavy rack a child climbs is a fall risk.
inputs: a shelf or high hook out of small hands' reach
wall anchors if the rack is tall and narrow
steps: Take every polish, cleaner and waterproofing spray off the rack and move them to a shelf above reach or out of the room.
Turn every shoe sole-down; nothing stands on its toe.
Move the heaviest pairs to the bottom shelf and the lightest to the top.
If the rack is tall and narrow, fix it to the wall so a climbing child cannot pull it forward.
Clear the floor between the door and the rack down to bare boards, a full stride wide.
cards.victory_condition: Shoe care solvents sit out of a toddler's reach, the rack cannot tip, and the floor between door and rack is bare.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a shoe rack fixed flush against a wall with a bare stretch of floor in front of it, a shelf well above head height holding shoe polish and cleaning bottles, out of a small child's reach
must_show: Shoe care solvents sit out of a toddler's reach, the rack cannot tip, and the floor between door and rack is bare.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: EMPTY THE DRAWER, KEEP THE DOOR TEST
cards.objective: Empty the drawer and keep only what you would want while wearing your outdoor shoes.
cards.why_it_matters: This drawer becomes the second junk drawer within a month of being emptied, every time, unless something is actually taken out rather than just tidied.
inputs: a box for things that belong in another room
steps: Tip the drawer out onto the bench and take out anything you would not want while wearing your outdoor shoes.
Give each removed item a real home elsewhere in the house, or let it go.
Wipe the seat and the top completely bare before putting the kept items back.
cards.victory_condition: Three items or fewer sit on the top, the seat is empty, and every drawer section holds one named category.

art.subject: an entry console with a mostly empty drawer holding a small handful of items and a bare seat and top surface above it
must_show: Three items or fewer sit on the top, the seat is empty, and every drawer section holds one named category.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: NAME THE DRAWER'S SECTIONS
cards.objective: Give every divided section of the drawer one named category so nothing new can drift in unchallenged.
cards.why_it_matters: A drawer with no named sections becomes the second junk drawer within a month, every time, because nothing tells the next loose item it does not belong.
inputs: small dividers or boxes that fit the drawer
a lidded tin for batteries and coins
steps: Take everything out of the drawer and group what earned its spot into like piles.
Fit a divider or small box for each pile, sized to the drawer.
Write one category name for each section, in your own words, and stick or write it where you will see it.
Put loose batteries, coins and small magnets into a lidded tin, not loose in a corner.
Wipe the seat and the top completely bare before putting the three kept items back.
cards.victory_condition: Every drawer section carries a name, batteries and coins sit inside a lidded tin, and the seat is completely bare.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: an open entry console drawer divided into labeled sections each holding one kind of small item, a lidded tin standing in one section holding batteries and coins
must_show: Every drawer section carries a name, batteries and coins sit inside a lidded tin, and the seat is completely bare.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR THE SWING AND CHECK THE MATS
cards.objective: Vacuum under both mats and clear anything stored inside the door's swing.
cards.why_it_matters: A flattened mat and something stored in the door's own swing are the two everyday ways this zone quietly stops doing its job.
steps: Lift both mats, vacuum the floor underneath, and check both faces of the inside mat for a flattened line where grit is riding across instead of catching.
Set both mats back down flat, corners uncurled.
Carry off anything at all sitting on the floor inside the door's swing.
cards.victory_condition: Both mats lie flat with no curled corners, and the floor inside the door's swing is bare.

art.subject: a front hallway with two mats vacuumed and lying flat and a completely bare stretch of floor in the door's swing
must_show: Both mats lie flat with no curled corners, and the floor inside the door's swing is bare.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: FIX THE DOOR AND TAPE THE OUTLINE
cards.objective: Tighten what makes the door and mats fail, and mark where each mat belongs so it stops drifting.
cards.why_it_matters: A loose hinge screw catches fingers, and a curled mat edge catches toes; both are cheap to fix and expensive to ignore.
inputs: a stiff brush or hose for the outdoor mat
steps: Tighten every visible hinge screw on the door while you are down at floor level.
Check the latch catches on the first push; adjust the strike plate if it does not.
Mark each mat's position on the floor with low tack tape so it always goes back the same way.
Brush or hose the outdoor mat clean and let it dry fully before it goes back down.
Confirm nothing at all sits on the floor inside the door's full swing.
cards.victory_condition: The door latches on the first push, both mats sit flat inside their taped outline, and the swing is completely bare.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a front door with a faint strip of tape on the floor marking a mat's outline just inside it, the mat sitting flat inside the taped line
must_show: The door latches on the first push, both mats sit flat inside their taped outline, and the swing is completely bare.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE SEASONAL SWAP
cards.objective: Move the outgoing season's coats, mats and gear out and the incoming season's in, on the day the weather actually turns.
cards.why_it_matters: Nothing marks the day the seasonal swap should happen, so it happens weeks late, wedged around what is already there.
inputs: a storage bin or bag for the outgoing season's gear
steps: On the first morning cold enough that you go looking for gloves, or warm enough that a coat feels wrong, do the swap standing there.
Take down every coat, pair of boots and accessory for the season that is ending.
Box or bag them and move them to storage in another room, not a shelf in this one.
Bring the incoming season's coats and shoes in and hang or rack them in the cleared space.
Swap the coarse outdoor mat for whichever grips better in the coming weather, if your entryway keeps two.
cards.victory_condition: Every coat and pair of shoes on display belongs to the current season, and last season's gear is stored elsewhere in the house.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a storage bin half packed with out-of-season coats sitting beside a coat rail that now holds only the current season's coats, spaced apart
must_show: Every coat and pair of shoes on display belongs to the current season, and last season's gear is stored elsewhere in the house.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FOURTEEN DAY PAPER RULE
cards.objective: Clear the folder down to nothing older than fourteen days, and act on or recycle every sheet past that line.
cards.why_it_matters: Paper in the folder without a deadline becomes furniture; the fourteen day line is what turns it back into a decision.
inputs: your phone, to pay or call while you are standing there
steps: Take the folder off the landing surface and go through it sheet by sheet.
Check the date written in the corner of each one against today.
Anything past fourteen days gets done right now, standing there: paid, signed, called, or recycled.
Write today's date on anything new that goes back in.
Put the folder back with nothing in it older than fourteen days.
cards.victory_condition: No sheet in the folder is older than fourteen days, and the ones that were have all been acted on or recycled.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a slim folder held open on an entryway console showing a handful of papers, a pen resting across the top sheet
must_show: No sheet in the folder is older than fourteen days, and the ones that were have all been acted on or recycled.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE FULL REBUILD WALK
cards.objective: Walk the whole entryway once, standing where you use it, and confirm nothing weighty, sharp, or wet is somewhere it could hurt someone.
cards.why_it_matters: The four things that hurt people in this room are height, weight, water and a door swing, and none of them show up unless you look on purpose.
inputs: nothing beyond thirty minutes and a working set of hands
steps: Stand at the console and check nothing heavy is stored above head height that could come down on someone reaching for a coat.
Check the charging dock and any lamp are clear of where a wet umbrella or coat would drip on them.
Check the shoe rack for anything that could tip, and confirm solvents sit out of a small child's reach.
Check both mats lie flat with no curled corner and the door latches on the first push.
Fix anything you find right there, or write it on the folder's top sheet with today's date if it needs a tool you do not have to hand.
cards.victory_condition: You can name, out loud, that height, drip, tip and trip have each been checked today.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a wide view of a whole entryway with a hand pointing at a coat hook, a shoe rack and a floor mat in turn, everything in its settled, put-away state
must_show: You can name, out loud, that height, drip, tip and trip have each been checked today.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LANDING ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: The surface holds the tray and the folder and nothing else, and keys never ride out of the house in a coat pocket that lives on a hanger.
cards.trigger: As you take your coat off, your hands are already full and already stopped. That is the moment everything in them goes into the tray.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Lift the tray, wipe the ring of dust underneath it, and set it back exactly where your hand opens on the way in.
Pull one sheet from the folder, give it its verdict right now, and write today's date on whatever goes back in.
Move the charging dock two inches clear of the drip line under the hooks and coil its cable flat.

art.subject: a narrow entryway console surface with one shallow tray holding two sets of keys and a pair of sunglasses, one wallet and one phone lying beside it, a slim upright folder holding a handful of papers standing at one end, and bare wood visible on both sides of the tray, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines

art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: COAT AND OUTERWEAR ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Two empty hooks at all times. If there is no empty hook, one coat is in the wrong room.
cards.trigger: On the first morning cold enough that you go looking for gloves, that is the seasonal swap. Do it that morning, standing there, rather than noting it for later.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Count the coats on the rail, and if both hooks nearest the door are full, carry one coat to a bedroom closet right now.
Straighten every coat hanger so shoulders sit square and no sleeve trails onto the floor.
Check the shelf above the rail for anything heavier than a hat, and move it down to a low shelf.

art.subject: a coat rail by a front door holding a small number of coats spaced apart with two hooks visibly empty at one end, a single bag hanging beside them, a labeled bin on the shelf above holding hats and gloves, and an umbrella stand with two umbrellas standing upright beside the rail, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: SHOE AND BOOT ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Two pairs per person at the door, soles down, everything else lives somewhere that is not the entryway.
cards.trigger: On the night the bins go out, the boot tray goes out with them and comes back empty.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Turn every pair on the rack sole-down and stand any pair lying on its side back upright.
Carry the boot tray outside, tip it out, and set it back down dry.
Pull one pair that is not on anyone's feet this season off the rack and carry it to its real home.

art.subject: a shoe rack beside a front door holding pairs of shoes standing on their soles with visible gaps between pairs, a low boot tray in front of it holding two pairs of boots standing upright, and a clear stretch of bare floor between the door and the rack wide enough for a full stride, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: ENTRY CONSOLE OR BENCH STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Three items on the top, an empty seat, and every drawer section holding one named category.
cards.trigger: You already open this drawer to put the dog lead back after a walk. While it is open, glance at the top and take it back to three.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Count what is on the top right now, and carry anything past three items straight to where it actually belongs.
Open the drawer and return one item that has drifted into the wrong named section.
Wipe the seat completely bare, even if you are about to sit something on it for thirty seconds.

art.subject: a narrow entry console with a bare wooden seat and exactly three small items sitting on its top surface, and a shallow open drawer below divided into sections, each holding one distinct kind of item with visible space around them, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: DOOR, MAT, AND IMMEDIATE FLOOR STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Nothing is stored on the floor inside the door's swing, ever, and both mats lie flat inside their taped outline.
cards.trigger: Whoever comes home last and locks the door straightens the mat with a foot before turning the key.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Press both mats flat with your foot, corner by corner, checking for any edge starting to curl.
Look at the floor inside the door's swing and carry off anything at all that has been set there.
Push the door shut and pull the handle once to confirm the latch caught on the first try.
